title: Which six digit number works in both directions?
description: A six digit number must be divisible by fifteen, and the number made by reversing its digits must be divisible by six. Fifteen needs the tests for three and five, six needs the tests for two and three, and reversing swaps the first and last digit and keeps the digit sum. A check by dividing confirms the number.
teaching_notes: One idea: reversing keeps the digit sum but swaps the first and last digit, so the units digit of each number decides the other number's test. Watch for students who test only the number and forget that its reverse needs an even last digit.

video_script.why: A learner combines the tests for three and five with the tests for two and three, and sees how reversing swaps the first and last digit and keeps the digit sum.
video_script.substitution: the book's own conditions: divisible by fifteen, reverse divisible by six
video_script.anchor: a six digit number with its first and last digit marked, and its reverse below it
video_script.payoff_line: Two lakh twenty five works, and its reverse is five lakh twenty thousand two.

final_answer.value: For example 200025 (reversed 520002); any number starting with an even digit, ending in 5, with digit sum a multiple of 3 works
final_answer.spoken: two lakh twenty five works, and its reverse is five lakh twenty thousand two

hold_back: For example 200025 (reversed 520002); any number starting with an even digit, ending in 5, with digit sum a multiple of 3 works
maths_rules: 15 = 3 × 5, so the number passes the test for 3 and the test for 5; the units digit is 0 or 5
6 = 2 × 3, so the reversed number passes the test for 2 and the test for 3
the units digit becomes the first digit when reversed; a 0 would make the reverse shorter than six digits, so the units digit is 5
the first digit becomes the units digit when reversed, so it must be even; choose 2
reversing keeps the digit sum; 2 + 5 = 7, and the middle digits 0, 0, 0, 2 add 2, so the digit sum is 9, a multiple of 3
video_script.design: One idea: use the tests for fifteen and six together with the reversal swap. Assumes the tests for two, three and five. The number and its reverse stay on the board all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a six digit number.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>It is divisible by fifteen. When its digits are reversed, the new number is divisible by six.
Which number can we write?

narration: <bookmark mark='tests'/>Fifteen is three times five, and six is two times three. We use the tests from your book.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>Reversing swaps the first digit and the last digit.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The digit sum stays the same.

beats.on_screen: Given: a 6-digit number divisible by 15 whose reverse is divisible by 6
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a six digit number divisible by fifteen, whose reverse is divisible by six.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write one number that does this.

beats.on_screen: Divisible by 15: tests for 3 and 5, so the units digit is 0 or 5. The units digit becomes the first digit when reversed; 0 would shorten it, so choose 5

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step one, divisible by fifteen means divisible by three and by five. The units digit must be zero or five.
<bookmark mark='swap'/>In the reversed number, the units digit becomes the first digit.
<bookmark mark='choose'/>A zero would make the reversed number shorter, so we choose five.

beats.on_screen: The reverse is divisible by 6: tests for 2 and 3. Its units digit is our first digit, so the first digit is even; choose 2

marks.rev: the reversed row is tagged tests for 2 and 3
marks.even: the first box of our number is tagged even
marks.choose: the first box is filled with 2

narration: <bookmark mark='rev'/>Step two, the reversed number must be divisible by two and by three.
<bookmark mark='even'/>Its units digit is the first digit of our number, so the first digit must be even.
<bookmark mark='choose'/>We choose two.

beats.on_screen: Digit sum is the same for both numbers. 2 + 5 = 7. Middle digits 0, 0, 0, 2 add 2, so the digit sum is 9, a multiple of 3. The number is 200025

marks.same: a note appears that one digit sum test covers both numbers
marks.mid: the middle boxes are filled with 0, 0, 0, 2 and the digit sum 9 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step three, reversing keeps the digit sum, so one digit sum test covers both numbers.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>The first and last digits, two and five, add to seven.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Choose the middle four digits as zero, zero, zero and two. The digit sum is nine, a multiple of three.

beats.on_screen: Check: 200025 ends in 5, digit sum 9, 200025 = 15 × 13335. Reverse 520002 is even, digit sum 9, 520002 = 6 × 86667

marks.num: 200025 ends in 5 and has digit sum 9

narration: <bookmark mark='num'/>Step four, check both numbers. Two lakh twenty five ends in five and its digit sum is nine, so fifteen divides it.
<bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Fifteen times thirteen thousand three hundred thirty five makes it.
<bookmark mark='rev'/>The reverse is five lakh twenty thousand two. It is even, and its digit sum is nine, so six divides it.
<bookmark mark='six'/>Six times eighty six thousand six hundred sixty seven makes it.
